lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: asking for clarification without hedging

objective: Learners rewrite a hedging, apology-heavy clarification request into a direct, respectful one that states exactly what is unclear and what they need, using a provided fictional unclear instruction as the scenario.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional, genuinely ambiguous workplace instruction, first drafts the hedging version they might naturally write ('sorry to bother you, this is probably a dumb question, but maybe...'), then rewrites it as a direct, respectful clarification request.
safetyNotes: The unclear instruction is fictional and provided with this lesson.

tasks.directions: Read the unclear instruction and write down, honestly, the hedging version you might naturally send.

prompts.text: Write your natural, hedging first-draft version, including any apologizing or self-doubting language you'd genuinely include.

tasks.directions: Rewrite it as a direct, respectful clarification request that states exactly what's unclear and what you need.

prompts.text: My rewrite removes unnecessary apologizing or self-doubting phrases.
My rewrite states exactly what part of the instruction is unclear.
My rewrite states exactly what I need to move forward (a specific answer or decision).

tasks.directions: Compare your hedging draft and your direct rewrite side by side, line by line, looking specifically at what changed in each sentence.

prompts.text: Name each hedging phrase you removed, and for each one explain specifically why removing it doesn't make the message rude, rather than just asserting that it doesn't.

tasks.directions: Reflect on the difference between hedging and being disrespectful.

prompts.text: Explain, in your own words, the difference between a direct message and a rude one, using your own rewrite as the example.

remediation: If a learner's rewrite still hedges heavily or swings too far into an abrupt, respect-lacking tone, reteach with a three-column model (hedging, disrespectful, direct-and-respectful) using one shared example sentence in all three columns, then have the learner revise their rewrite to match the direct-and-respectful column.
extension: Have the learner write a version of the same clarification request for a much more time-sensitive situation, and explain what changes when urgency is added without losing respect.
